description:
Test-strategy review of the write_primitives and dataframe-runner unit
suites found several places where tests assert shapes/mocks rather than
values, so they cannot catch real regressions:

1. `tests/unit/core/write_primitives/test_pyspark_sketch_factories.py`
   mocks the whole PySpark API (`fake_pyspark_functions` fixture,
   `MagicMock()` spark session) and mostly asserts call shapes (e.g.
   lines ~92-96, ~106, ~146-147). The one apparent "value" assertion,
   `TestPysparkHllMergeExtract.test_extractor_reads_state_and_chains_union_then_estimate`
   (line ~117-130), configures `row.__getitem__.return_value = 14836.5`
   and then asserts `result == 14836.5` — the assertion is tautological
   because the value only ever flows out of the same mock it was injected
   into; the extractor's real logic (indexing into the Row by a specific
   column key) is never verified.

2. `tests/unit/core/write_primitives/test_benchmark_execution.py` has 7
   tests (lines 206, 360, 374, 390, 404, 418, 591) that end on
   `mock_conn.execute.assert_not_called()` with no accompanying positive
   assertion about the resulting state (e.g. what error/skip/no-op result
   was actually produced). "Execute was never called" alone doesn't
   verify the surrounding code behaved correctly — a test that returns
   early for the wrong reason still passes.

3. `tests/unit/core/runner/test_dataframe_runner.py:484`
   (`test_standard_phase_does_not_raise`) asserts
   `result.validation_status in ("PASSED", "FAILED")`. This is an
   either-outcome assertion: both possible values pass, so a regression
   that flips the actual outcome is invisible. Tracing the runner
   (`benchbox/core/runner/dataframe_runner.py`): the result builder
   defaults `_validation_status` to `"PASSED"`
   (`benchbox/core/results/builder.py:261`) and only overwrites it to
   `"FAILED"` in the runner's `except` branch (dataframe_runner.py:298-303)
   or to `"PARTIAL"` when failed queries exist and status was still
   `"PASSED"` (builder.py:598-600). Since this test runs with
   `DataFramePhases(load=False, execute=False)` and a mocked adapter that
   raises nothing, the only reachable outcome is `"PASSED"` — the
   assertion should be pinned to that. (Note: the review that seeded this
   TODO cited "lines ~464,486" for this pattern; only line 484 actually
   contains it — line 464 is an unrelated `NotImplementedError` test and
   line 486 (`test_power_phase_does_not_raise`) only checks
   `isinstance(result, BenchmarkResults)`, not `validation_status`.)

4. `tests/unit/benchmarks/test_write_primitives_dataframe.py` has 12
   in-body `try: from ... import X / except ImportError: pytest.skip(...)`
   sites (e.g. lines ~566, 586, 610, 622, 639, 691, 758, 809, 862, 928,
   950, 972), all guarding imports from
   `benchbox.platforms.dataframe.pyspark_maintenance`. PySpark is a core
   (non-optional) dependency of this project
   (`pyspark>=3.5.0` in `pyproject.toml`'s main `dependencies` list, not
   an extra), so it is installed in CI. These in-body skips mean that if
   a future change breaks the import of the module under test (e.g. a
   typo, a moved symbol, a real ImportError from a genuinely broken
   dependency chain), the tests silently skip instead of failing — CI
   stays green.

None of these are found-then-forgotten: they're passing tests today that
would keep passing through the regressions they're nominally guarding
against.

anti_patterns.dont: convert test_benchmark_execution.py's assert_not_called() tests into full integration tests with a real connection
anti_patterns.instead: keep them mock-based, just add a positive assertion on the mocked result/state.
anti_patterns.why: that's out of scope and would require live DB fixtures

anti_patterns.dont: delete the mock-based call-shape assertions in test_pyspark_sketch_factories.py
anti_patterns.instead: only fix the tautological value assertion(s), leave the rest.
anti_patterns.why: they correctly verify chaining/argument behavior for a fully-mocked PySpark API

anti_patterns.dont: move the module-level importorskip for test_write_primitives_dataframe.py into conftest.py
anti_patterns.instead: keep the guard local to this file.
anti_patterns.why: other test files in the same directory import unrelated platforms and would be needlessly skipped

anti_patterns.dont: weaken test_dataframe_runner.py:484 further (e.g. to `is not None`)
anti_patterns.why: the whole point is pinning the actually-reachable value

preserves.behavior: All 7 test_benchmark_execution.py assert_not_called() calls remain in place - only add assertions, don't remove existing ones.
No change to production code in benchbox/core/write_primitives/, benchbox/core/runner/, or benchbox/platforms/dataframe/ - this is a test-only TODO.
Tests still skip cleanly (not error) on developer machines without PySpark installed, via the module-level importorskip/import-guard, not per-test try/except.

verifications.description: PySpark sketch factory tests still pass after de-tautologizing the value assertion
Benchmark execution tests still pass with added positive assertions
DataFrame runner test passes with the pinned validation_status
Write-primitives dataframe tests still pass and no longer skip on PySpark import (since PySpark is installed)
verifications.expected: Tests pass (not skipped) since pyspark is a core dependency and is installed

work_units.notes:
In `TestPysparkHllMergeExtract.test_extractor_reads_state_and_chains_union_then_estimate`
(~line 113-130), the assertion `assert result == 14836.5` merely
echoes `row.__getitem__.return_value` set two lines earlier — replace
or strengthen it so the test verifies the extractor's actual logic:
  - Assert `row.__getitem__.call_args == call(0)` (or whichever key/
    index the extractor is documented to read) so the test would fail
    if the extractor started reading the wrong column/index.
  - Where the full-mock architecture makes a fully "real" value
    assertion infeasible (no real PySpark Row available in this unit
    test), use a small hand-built fake Row class (e.g. a
    `dict`-backed object implementing `__getitem__`) instead of
    `MagicMock`, so `result` is produced by genuine dict lookup logic
    in the extractor rather than being an injected mock return value.
Apply the same "real/fake-backed value, not injected-mock-echo"
pattern to any other value-bearing assertions in this file that
exhibit the same tautology (skim the KLL and top-K merge-extract
tests for the same `row.__getitem__.return_value = X; assert result
== X` shape).
Leave the call-shape assertions (e.g. `assert_called_once_with(...)`)
as-is where they already verify real behavior (arguments, chaining).
work_units.summary: test_pyspark_sketch_factories.py: fix the tautological HLL-merge-extract value assertion

work_units.notes:
For each of the 7 tests ending on `mock_conn.execute.assert_not_called()`
(lines 206, 360, 374, 390, 404, 418, 591), read the surrounding test to
determine what SHOULD have happened instead of executing SQL (e.g. an
early-return value, a raised/logged error, a specific `OperationResult`
state, a skip reason). Add an assertion on that positive outcome so the
test fails if the code takes the "don't execute" path for the wrong
reason. Do not weaken or remove the `assert_not_called()` calls
themselves — they stay as a necessary (not sufficient) condition.
work_units.summary: test_benchmark_execution.py: add positive assertions alongside the 7 execute.assert_not_called() sites

work_units.summary: test_dataframe_runner.py:484: pin validation_status to PASSED for this fixture

work_units.notes:
Replace the 12 in-body `try/except ImportError: pytest.skip(...)`
sites (~lines 566, 586, 610, 622, 639, 691, 758, 809, 862, 928, 950,
972) that guard imports from
`benchbox.platforms.dataframe.pyspark_maintenance` with a single
module-level `pyspark = pytest.importorskip("pyspark")`-style guard
(or, since the failure mode is specifically the BenchBox wrapper
module rather than the `pyspark` package itself, guard on
`benchbox.platforms.dataframe.pyspark_maintenance` directly) placed
once near the top of the file, alongside the existing module-level
`except ImportError` block at lines 21/29. This preserves "skip
cleanly on machines without PySpark installed" for local dev while
ensuring a genuine breakage of the module under test (which PySpark
IS installed to exercise in CI - see `pyproject.toml`'s core
`dependencies` list) fails the suite instead of silently skipping.
Keep the two existing legitimate module-level import guards (lines
21, 29) - only remove the in-body per-test duplicates.
